extracted.intended_audience: readers of voyage/natural-history narratives; naturalists, surveyors, and geographers
extracted.subtask_description: First‑person voyage and field‑notes combining coastal surveying, natural history (flora/fauna), geology, tidal and meteorological observations, and brief anthropological remarks collected during a naval voyage. Emphasises empirical measurements, specimen collection, and interpretive generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise positions and bearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Give exact latitudes and longitudes and compass bearings for observations and features (e.g. "latitude 32 degrees 27 minutes 21 seconds South and longitude 2 degrees 1 minute 10 seconds West of Swan River, variation 4 degrees 10 minutes westerly").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include variation, bearings of features from landmarks (e.g. 'Record Hill bearing North 70 degrees East six miles and a half'), distances to features (miles), and reference points (e.g. 'West Wallaby Island bearing...'). Precise positional data enable verification and charting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide tidal observations (times, rises/falls, durations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report times of high‑water (e.g. 'time of high-water at the full and change was six o'clock when the tide rose 30 inches'), rises and falls, and durations of flood and ebb.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present series of observations (number of observations noted), distinguish full/change vs neap conditions, note day/night differences in flood/ebb durations and amplitudes, and quantify rises/falls (in inches or feet). Mention any anomalous patterns and the number of observations supporting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report depth soundings and bottom composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Give depth measurements in fathoms and describe the nature of the bottom encountered (e.g. '122 fathoms, sand and coral'; 'fine grey sandy mud or marl').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sounding depths at locations, note presence/absence of bottom at extreme leads (e.g. 'no bottom with 200 and 240 fathoms'), and characterize substrate (sand, coral, shells, marl). Use soundings to infer banks, reefs, and navigable channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe anchorage, navigational hazards and approach details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide harbour/anchorage descriptions including leading marks, reefs, coral patches, depths at entrance and inside, and sheltered aspects (e.g. Recruit Harbour: 'In entering we had 7 and 8 fathoms, but the depth inside is 11 and 12; it is perfectly sheltered on all sides').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give bearings and visible marks that lead into harbour, note positions of spits, reefs that dry at low water, safe depths for approach, and any local hazards; specify which sides are sheltered. Such practical details are essential for navigation and anchoring decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document species: counts, specimens, behavior, and naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Record numbers and weights of animals taken (e.g. 'on one day... I shot 36, and that between three guns we killed 76, averaging in weight about seven pounds each'), new species identifications (e.g. 'described... as Halmaturus houtmannii'), and behavioural notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts, average weights, locality where specimens were obtained, behavioural observations (voracity, attachment, burrowing), and any taxonomic naming or reference to describers (e.g. Mr. Gould). Note preservation methods and provenance of type specimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide geological and geomorphological descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe rock types, formations, stratigraphy and geomorphology (e.g. 'Flag Hill is a rock formed of sand and comminuted shells; the flat ... is of limestone formation'; 'columnar blocks of the greenstone').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record visible lithology, layering, soil sections from wells or pits (depths and composition), island profiles, reef connectivity, and any inferences about banks or continental connections. Mention characteristic forms (pyramidal hills, sandhills) and their elevations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include meteorological observations and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Report weather, winds, temperatures and atmospheric optical effects (e.g. 'fierce south-east breeze', 'temperature... reduced to 59 degrees', 'effect of the treacherous mirage').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State prevailing wind directions/timing (e.g. morning south winds veering east), seasonal/astronomical correlations (e.g. winds stronger at full/change of moon), temperature measurements, and describe how conditions (light winds, mirage) altered perception of the land and impeded progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe indigenous material culture and art with interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record native drawings, methods of making them, subjects, and interpretations (e.g. 'they do this by removing the hard red outer coating... Much ability is displayed... the subjects of which could be discovered at a glance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts and types of motifs, method of manufacture, contextual notes (location, seasonality), and considered reflections on their significance (comparison with other art traditions, absence of indecency). Include illustrative lists or figure captions when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report elevations, distances and island extents
rubrics_metrics.description: Give heights of hills/sandhills, breadth/length of islands, and distances between groups (e.g. 'greatest height is 12 feet', 'Flag Hill... measures no more than 50 feet', 'Abrolhos extend... forty-eight miles').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric elevations (feet), island dimensions (miles), widths of channels, and spatial relationships between groups. Use these measurements to characterise island groups and to assist charting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide visual documentation (sketches, lithographs, plates) and figure lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Include drawings and lithographic impressions of observations with captions and numbered lists (e.g. 'Lithographic impression of the copies made by Captain Wickham... The following list will convey...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or reference plates/sketches, number and caption figures, and list what each figure represents. Use sketches for species, native art, and coastal profiles to complement textual description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe field methods, specimen handling, and collection logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain methods of obtaining samples, preserving specimens, digging wells and making soundings (e.g. sample placed 'in a wide-mouthed bottle with some spirits' and later broken; 'sank wells... at the depth of twenty-one feet the water... was salt').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the techniques, instruments (boats, sounding leads, wells), preservation media (spirits), storage and transport arrangements, and note accidents or losses as cautionary examples. Detail effort required (carrying water in seven-gallon barrels) and labour costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give rationale for place names and toponyms
rubrics_metrics.description: State the names given to features and the reason for those names (e.g. 'harbour we named Recruit Harbour, from its affording fresh supplies of the small kangaroo'; 'Flag Hill... Fish Point, from the number of snappers we caught there').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When naming, explain the descriptive or anecdotal basis (resources, events, features). This documents local history of the voyage and helps later users understand name origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make general inferential remarks linking observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer hypotheses and generalizations derived from repeated observations (e.g. 'the reefs are compact in proportion to the exposed position of the islands'; 'they are not connected with each other, but rest on the outer extremity of a level or bank').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesize local data (soundings, reef patterns, substrate) into broader statements about geology, biogeography, or hydrology, while noting the evidence and limits of inference. Use repeated, corroborated observations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document logistical and subsistence considerations (water, food, transport)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record searches and procurement of essentials (e.g. 'search for the stream... dug as many as eight [wells]... Mr. Bynoe found a reservoir... we got about six tons of tolerable water'; 'thirty green turtles were brought on board').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sources and quantities of potable water, food resources available (fish, turtles, kangaroos), methods of transport and carrying loads, and the labour involved. Note limitations that affect the duration and safety of shore operations.
